bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: James Harris "Jim" Simons (April 25, 1938 – May 10, 2024) was an American mathematician, hedge fund manager, and philanthropist. The only child of Matthew Simons and Marcia (Kantor) Simons, he was raised in Brookline, Massachusetts until moving to Newton, Massachusetts in 1952. After graduating from Newton High School, Simons attended MIT, where he graduated in 1958 with a Bachelor of Science. After initially pursuing graduate work at MIT, Simons received a PhD in Mathematics from UC Berkeley in 1962. His doctoral thesis, "On the Transitivity of Holonomy Systems," was advised by Bertram Kostant.

Following his doctorate, Simons taught at MIT for one year. He then spent time in Bogotá, Columbia to start a floor-tile business, before returning to academia in the United States in 1963 to teach at Harvard. From 1964 to 1968, in addition to teaching at MIT and Harvard, Simons worked as a code breaker for the Communications Research Division of the Institute for Defense Analyses in Princeton, New Jersey. [Simons left the IDA after writing a letter to the New York Times critical of the Vietnam War.] Simons chaired the math department at Stony Brook University from 1968 to 1978. During this time, his collaboration with the mathematician Shiing-Shen Chern resulted in the discovery of the Chern-Simons form, described in the 1974 paper "Characteristic Forms and Geometric Invariants," which would later be recognized for its significance to theoretical physics.

In 1978, Simons resigned from Stony Brook and founded Monemetrics, which was renamed Renaissance Technologies in 1982. The hedge fund formed the Medallion Fund in 1988, which achieved among the highest annual returns among any hedge fund in history. The success of Renaissance Technologies made Simons extremely wealthy. Simons retired as CEO of Renaissance Technologies in 2010 and served as chairman until 2021.

Simons and his wife Marilyn Simons founded the Simons Foundation in 1994, which is a major funder of work on mathematics and basic sciences. In 2004, Simons founded Math for America, a nonprofit which supports STEM teachers in New York City. Simons was active in philanthropy work, including starting other foundations and serving on the boards of numerous organizations, especially those with a focus on math and science. Simons was the recipient of numerous awards, including the Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy, which he received along with Marilyn in 2013.
Simons was married twice and had five children. His first marriage, to Barbara Bluestein, lasted from 1959 to 1974. He married Marilyn Hawrys in 1977, remaining married until his death in 2024.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The James Simons papers consist of material related to Simons' professional activities, personal life, and philanthropic work. The collection includes awards, mathematical course and research notes, personal correspondence, personal press clippings, photographs, subject files, and audiovisual recordings from throughout Simons' life, but particularly from the 1990s and later. The collection includes material collected after Simons' death, including memorial publications and condolence emails to Marilyn Simons. No business records or materials related to Simons' investments are included in the collection.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is arranged in four series, each of which contains multiple sub-series.
Sub-series 2.6 Photographs and Video, c. 1920s – 2024, undated
Sub-series 2.8 Speeches, Writings, and Oral Histories, c. 1960s – 2024, undated
Sub-series 3.2 Mathematical Research Notes, c. 1956 – 2024, undated

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: The collection was significantly rearranged and physically rehoused during processing. Photographs were removed from albums. Duplicates beyond two copies were disposed of. Subject and correspondence files were generally kept in their original files and were significantly weeded. Condolence cards without substantive information about James Simons were not included in this collection. A facsimile of the 50th Birthday Scrapbook was created; the original scrapbook is not included in the collection. Mathematics notebooks were reviewed by mathematicians and assigned titles based on an assessment of their subject matter.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: The MJS Foundation has legal title, copyright, and literary property rights to the James Simons papers in so far as it holds them. Rockefeller Archive Center has authority to grant permission to cite and publish archival material from the collection.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: The MJS Foundation deposited the James Simons papers at Rockefeller Archive Center in 2025.

scopecontent.p: This series contains materials related to Simons' involvement with businesses, particularly Monemetrics and Renaissance Technologies. The bulk of the series consists of media profiles of Simons focused on his investing success and photographs from company parties and events. The series does not contain any business records.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series documents the personal life and public legacy of Simons. The series contains awards, correspondence, photographs, media coverage, and personal memorabilia, including records of academic and professional achievements, family photographs, genealogical records, and personal writings and speeches. Condolences were written to Marilyn Simons after Simons' death.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This sub-series contains diplomas, awards, certificates given to Simons recognizing academic and other achievements. Resolutions by MIT and Stony Brook were issued to recognize Simons after his death. Some files include additional correspondence or other materials related to the awards. Materials are arranged chronologically.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This sub-series contains condolence letters, notes, and emails written following Simons' death, as well as memorials and tributes to Simons. Condolences include letters and emails addressed to Marilyn Simons as well as handwritten notes collected by the Simons Foundation and emails sent to a public email address administered by the Foundation. Memorials consist of published tributes in academic journals and organizational communications. Additionally, the sub-series contains one folder of personal anecdotes about Simons written down and collected by Marilyn Simons.

scopecontent.p: This sub-series contains three-dimensional awards, objects, and clothing. Objects and awards in the sub-series are medals given to Simons, a gift marking his 80th birthday, and poker chips from multiple years of Wall Street Poker Night events. Clothing includes Simons' "magic tie" and academic hoods.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This sub-series contains a physical and digital photographs of James Simons and others from a variety of sources. Photographs include family photographs of Simons and relations (both originals and reproductions), portrait photographs of Simons, photographs from events which Simons attended and spoke at, and in other contexts. Videos include interviews and oral history recordings, and recordings from birthday parties, galas, and graduation ceremonies in which Simons spoke or took part. Materials are arranged chronologically.

scopecontent.p: Sub-series 2.9 Subject Files: This sub-series contains a small number of subject files unrelated to business, math, or philanthropy. These include records of Simon's boats, political advocacy, and a 2003 trip to Nepal.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains records related to Simons' mathematical work and career as a mathematician. Course and research notes consist of notes from mathematics classes taken by Simons at MIT, notes used for classes taught by Simons, mathematical research in notebooks and close notes. Additional material in the series includes correspondence, a limited amount of photographs and video, and copies of mathematical papers co-authored by Simons.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This sub-series consists of correspondence to and from Simons in his capacity as Chair of the Stony Brook University Department of Mathematics, covering academic and administrative matters, including student and faculty recruitment records. The sub-series also contains four files related to Simon's collaboration with Dennis Sullivan, consisting of correspondence and handwritten mathematical research notes by Simons.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This sub-series contains mathematical course notes and research notes, as well as notes on card games. Course notes include notebooks containing notes on courses taken by Jim Simons at MIT; and notebooks, loose notes, and notes in binders which appear to be related to unidentified math courses taken by and taught by Simons. Mathematical research notes consist of handwritten mathematical work by Simons on multiple subjects, not clearly identified as related to specific papers.

scopecontent.p: This series contains materials related to Simons' philanthropy, including photographs and video of Simons at events celebrating his philanthropy, subject files related to various organizations, and media coverage focused on his philanthropy. The sub-series also includes three publications in book format commemorating Simons' donations and new initiatives supported by the Simons Foundation.
